templates.source:
subject: [[your invoices, and a guess about where the hours came from | which of your four tools is right about the scope? | the friday timesheet]]

Hi {first_name|there},

{first_name|This address} is listed on the {company_name} site((, as {title})).

Somebody at {company_name} typed the same scope into a fourth tool this week. It went into the proposal, then the SOW, then the project tool, then the invoice, and the hours on the invoice came from a timesheet filled in on Friday from memory. Nobody owns the whole chain, so when the scope moves, one of the four stays wrong until the client points it out.

One new project is four setups and one change order is four edits, and every one of those hours lands on the timesheet as admin, which never reaches an invoice.

The invoice is the worst of it. The hours on it don't match the timesheet, the timesheet doesn't match the SOW, and whoever notices either eats the difference or has the awkward call with the client. Have fun with the retyping and the "which one is right" emails.

You could build the fix yourselves, and I'll get to why you haven't after a line about who I am.

I'm William, from Wren Automation. I'm a software engineering student at the University of Waterloo, and this is the business I'm building. My work has been data cleaning, pipelines that connect systems, and CRMs. Two things I've built: an internal policy chatbot for the Government of Canada, which 17,000 staff use instead of searching 220+ directives by hand, saving about 6 to 7 hours a week each. And a University of Alberta lab tool that cut 200+ hours of manual lookups across 7,000+ records of messy fuel cell data, terabytes of it, in outdated file types.

The fix is a quiet week where someone on the team wires it up. You know that, which is why it has been on the list for two years and every quiet week went to a client. At a small scale this might not matter, but with the number of projects you guys run at once it's hours a week per person.

If you're interested, reply with a few times that work and I'll book it. First step is a free consultation and an audit of where the retyping happens. You get one page back, where the hours go and what to fix first, and it's yours whether or not we build anything.

Thanks for reading this far.

Best,
William

Hi {first_name|there},

{first_name|This address} is listed on the {company_name} site((, as {title})).

Somebody at {company_name} typed the same client into a fifth tool this week. The deal went into the CRM, the project into the project tool, the hours into a timesheet on Friday from memory, the invoice got built from the timesheet, and the check-in notes went into a doc. Nobody owns the whole chain, so when a contact or the scope changes, one of the five stays wrong until the client points it out.

One new client is five setups and one scope change is five edits, and every one of those hours lands on the timesheet as admin, which never reaches an invoice.

Month end is the worst of it. The numbers come out of the ad accounts and the analytics into a spreadsheet, someone fixes them by hand and pastes them into the deck, and one client gets last month's number. The report lands a day late and the first reply is about the wrong number. Have fun with the retyping and the "which number is right" emails.

The zap someone set up didn't fix it either, and I'll say why after a line about who I am.

I'm William, from Wren Automation. I'm a software engineering student at the University of Waterloo, and this is the business I'm building. My work has been data cleaning, pipelines that connect systems, and CRMs. Two things I've built: an internal policy chatbot for the Government of Canada, which 17,000 staff use instead of searching 220+ directives by hand, saving about 6 to 7 hours a week each. And a University of Alberta lab tool that cut 200+ hours of manual lookups across 7,000+ records of messy fuel cell data, terabytes of it, in outdated file types.

The zap is the usual fix. Someone wired one up between the CRM and the project tool and it worked, until someone renamed a field and it had been failing for three weeks before anyone noticed. Or the person who set it up left. At a small scale this might not matter, but with the number of clients you guys run at once it's hours a week per person.

If you're interested, reply with a few times that work and I'll book it. First step is a free consultation and an audit of where the retyping happens. You get one page back, where the hours go and what to fix first, and it's yours whether or not we build anything.

Thanks for reading this far.

Best,
William

templates.name: documents/followup
templates.source:
Hi {first_name|there},

Just checking you saw my last email. If not, skip it unless you have been having issues keeping track of your documents and data in a clean, principled way (think copy pasting back and forth between 5 different spreadsheets. If that's you, this email should be of interest to you).

Something you can use whether or not we talk more: Microsoft Document Intelligence. Point it at your Part 1 and your 2A and it reads both into tables. subject: [[read your form adv, one guess about your documents | how many documents hold your aum number? | your documents, and a guess about where they break]]

Hi {first_name|there},

Your name is on the Form ADV for {company_name}((, which lists you as {title})).

You've definitely experienced this: your numbers move between documents by hand. Pulled, pasted into a spreadsheet one person owns, passed on. No version history, and one edit breaks something two tabs over. Every amendment, someone re-reads all of it to check. One example: your AUM figure sits in Part 1, the 2A, the supplements, the CRS and the compliance manual. ((Your last filing says {company.aum}. After the next amendment, all five have to catch up. Have fun with the manual edits and the mental bookkeeping.))

I'm William, from Wren Automation. I'm a software engineering student at the University of Waterloo, and this is the business I'm building. My work has been data cleaning, pipelines that connect systems, and CRMs. Two things I've built: an internal policy chatbot for the Government of Canada, which 17,000 staff use instead of searching 220+ directives by hand, saving about 6 to 7 hours a week each. And   a University of Alberta lab tool that cut 200+ hours of manual lookups across 7,000+ records of messy fuel cell data, terabytes of it, in outdated file types.

The usual fix is being careful and a checklist. It works until years down the a line a new hire gets complacent, or you do. The compliance platform stores the documents and reminds you what's due, but it doesn't notice when two of them drift apart. At a small scale, this might not matter, but its burning hours of your time every week with the amount of data you guys handle.

If you're interested, reply with a few times that work and I'll book it. First step is a free consultation and a proper audit of where your numbers move by hand, and we'll go from there.

Thanks for reading this far.

Best,
William

Hi {first_name|there},

Your name is on the Form ADV for {company_name}((, which lists you as {title})).

You've definitely experienced this: the same client data typed by hand into system after system. Onboarding into the CRM, the custodian forms, the portfolio system, the planning tool. Same name, address, date of birth and beneficiaries, four times. Then the quarterly pull, exported from three of them into one spreadsheet and fixed by hand. ((With {company.ind_clients} clients, that's real hours.)) Have fun with the retyping and the "which one is right" emails.

I'm William, of Wren Automation. I'm a software engineering student at the University of Waterloo, and this is the business I'm building. And a University of Alberta lab tool that cut 200+ hours of manual lookups across 7,000+ records of messy fuel cell data, terabytes of it, in outdated file types.

The usual fix is a good ops person and a checklist. It works until that person is the bottleneck. The "integration" is a nightly CSV that breaks when two fields disagree.

If you're interested, reply with a few times that work and I'll book it. First step is a free consultation and a proper audit of where the retyping happens. We go from there.

Thanks for reading this far.

Best,
William
